contracts.text:
# Rating summary: supplied read-only display

`rating-summary` is an original implementation of a read-only rating-summary presentation. A single solid decorative star precedes the supplied rating label and an optional muted review-count label in one horizontal, non-wrapping row. With a provider, the whole row is a native source link. It does not collect a user's rating or verify a review service.

The separate [`rating`](rating.md) node remains a project-local controlled input extension with its existing wire contract and behavior.

## Contract

- `type`: `"rating-summary"`
- `ratingLabel`: required literal string, 1–200 Unicode code points
- `reviewCountLabel`: optional literal string, 1–200 Unicode code points
- `provider`: optional object requiring `label` (literal string, 1–200 Unicode code points) and `url` (literal string, 1–2,048 Unicode code points)
- `id`: the ordinary optional node identifier

All objects are closed. Numeric values, state expressions, `bind`, editable controls, arbitrary markup, custom star counts, provider logos, image URLs, callbacks and alternate protocols are unsupported. Labels are rendered as text, including HTML-looking text. Hosts supply punctuation and localization explicitly; the renderer does not parse, round, translate or append units to the labels.

Omitting `reviewCountLabel` omits that text entirely. An unknown count may be represented by an explicit literal such as `"Review count unavailable"`. Neither omission nor an unknown label becomes `0 reviews`. Similarly, the renderer does not invent a rating when an author supplies `"Not rated"`.

See the original [example](../examples/rating-summary.json). The isolated schema module is `content/rating-summary`; it recognizes only this node and its declared shared document dependencies.

## Link, accessibility and layout semantics

Without `provider`, the row is ordinary non-focusable text. With `provider`, one native anchor contains the star, rating, review count when supplied, and the visible provider label. It uses the browser's ordinary same-tab navigation, `rel="noreferrer"` and `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"`. The anchor's accessible name comes from all its literal text. No custom click or keyboard handler overrides native link behavior.

The provider URL must be absolute HTTP(S) and pass the shared `isSafeURL` policy. Relative, credential-bearing, script, data, browser-internal, `mailto:`, `tel:` and fragment-only destinations are rejected by full validation. Structural schema selection alone does not establish URL safety; run `validateDocument` before mounting or compiling.

The single star is hidden from assistive technology; it is not a checkbox, radio, slider, image description or numeric range. Text labels use independent bidirectional isolation, while the row follows the renderer root's resolved writing direction. The root uses its existing `dir="auto"` behavior: language metadata alone does not force RTL, and isolated labels do not determine their ancestor's direction. An RTL document can supply ordinary RTL text such as its description. Narrow containers keep one row and truncate long visible labels with ellipses. Full literal text remains in the DOM, accessible link name and each label's native title. The link has a visible keyboard-focus outline. No synthetic input, form participation, live region, state subscription or change event is introduced.

## Provenance and verification boundary

The renderer, silhouette and examples are independently authored project code. No private reference source, screenshot, provider logo or third-party brand asset is included. Provider branding via remote or inline images is not supported in this contract. The visible provider label is a plain-text attribution chosen by the document author.

Supplied ratings, review counts and provider identities are unverified author data. A source link makes no claim about accuracy, freshness, trust, an endorsement, or a successful online lookup. Mounting and offline compilation introduce no network fetch, metadata lookup, storage, timer or tracking.

`tests/rating-summary.test.mjs` covers bounded schema fields and types, exact literal rendering, missing and unknown counts, safe URLs, link semantics, accessibility structure, unchanged interactive rating behavior, lifecycle and deterministic offline compilation. `tests/browser/rating-summary.spec.mjs` is prepared for real-browser verification of native keyboard links, single-row layout, narrow containers, RTL, themes, forced colors and reduced motion. Browser, screen-reader and pixel acceptance should be claimed only after those checks have actually run.

## 状态与表达式

`state` 保存字符串、有限数值或布尔值。引用写作 `{ "$": "gain" }`，计算写作 `{ "op": "mul", "args": [12, { "$": "gain" }] }`。

可用操作符：`add`、`sub`、`mul`、`div`、`max`、`min`、`round`、`abs`、`clamp`、`gt`、`lt`、`eq`、`if`、`format`。它们是受约束的数据树，不是 JavaScript 源码。未知引用、循环依赖、非法参数、除零及非有限结果会被拒绝。

需要直接求值时，可从主入口导入 `evaluateValue` 和 `evaluateState`；通常由控件与渲染器自动处理即可。

# API and security model

`iui/1` is data, never executable source. Content text is inserted through text nodes. The only HTML sink is KaTeX's generated visual HTML plus accessible MathML with `trust:false`, bounded expansion/size, and strict parsing; model HTML never enters that sink directly. Unsupported TeX falls back to visible source.

## Validation

The JSON Schema is generated from `scripts/generate-schema.mjs`. TypeScript declarations and the Ajv standalone validator are generated in the same step. CI rejects drift. Browser code imports the already generated validator, avoiding runtime `new Function` and allowing a script hash CSP without `unsafe-eval`.

`validateDocument(input)` returns `{ok:true,document}` or `{ok:false,issues}`. It accepts plain JSON values only; custom prototypes, accessors, cyclic objects, reserved keys, nonfinite numbers, and excessive values/text/depth are rejected before Ajv traversal. Semantics additionally reject unknown references, computed cycles, bad operator arities/types, numerical errors, duplicate IDs, unknown state bindings, broken topology endpoints, malformed table widths, invalid chart data, and unsafe resource declarations.

`evaluateValue(value,state,computed)` evaluates a constrained expression and throws on invalid input. `evaluateState(document,override)` returns validated, frozen state/computed results or issues. Controller state updates use this checked path. Numeric operators do not coerce strings. `if` is lazy at evaluation but both branches are inspected for references and types; runtime arithmetic errors still reject the state transition.

Limits include 64 JSON nesting levels, 2,000 node-like objects, 50,000 values, a two-million-UTF-16-code-unit text budget (including JSON keys, retained across merged state updates), and schema-specific row/series/child limits. These limits reduce resource exhaustion; they are not a promise of fixed latency for every valid document.

## Browser boundary

No raw HTML, CSS, JS, callback, import, network action, form submission, or arbitrary AppBlock is accepted. SVG uses a fixed shape list and numeric/color/geometry attribute allowlists. `native` is recognized solely to report `UNSUPPORTED_NATIVE`. It does not load an adapter.

Model URLs are limited to the documented link/image policy. Remote images require a reader action and use no-referrer. URLs still lead to third parties when a reader activates them; validation does not certify the destination's content or privacy. Callers handling confidential documents should avoid remote URLs altogether.

Compiled inline HTML applies a CSP containing the exact SHA-256 of its runtime. It blocks network connections, objects, forms, base URL changes, and remote scripts/fonts; font-src data: permits the bundled official WOFF2 fonts. Styles allow inline rules because the renderer writes bounded, host-owned numeric/enum properties. The host browser's CSP remains authoritative for `mount`; pass `styles:false` and serve the stylesheet when embedding under a stricter host policy.

`compileHtml(input,{assets:'inline',backend:'portable',lang})` emits one self-contained HTML file. `compileArtifact(input,{assets:'shared',assetBase:'./iui-assets/',lang})` also returns an asset map with safe relative file paths. Shared output is intended for a static HTTP server; no claim is made for every browser's file-origin shared-script policy. Both reject unsupported backends.

## Lifecycle and scope

Controllers isolate state. `update` validates the complete next document and resets state. `setState` merges a scalar patch, verifies all bindings and derived values, then updates existing nodes without replacing focused controls. `dispose` is idempotent and removes its owned elements, listeners, and resize observer. External DOM edits by the embedding host are outside this contract.

The library does not authenticate users, persist documents, store credentials, run simulations as scientific truth, fetch sources, or verify model-generated facts. Applications remain responsible for provenance, permissions, and their host threat model.

JSON Schema string `maxLength` and evaluated Value/state string maxima use Unicode code points. A Value string accepts at most 12,000 code points, including astral characters, while the independent whole-document resource budget still counts UTF-16 storage units. The resolved evaluation context (state, computed scalars and the evaluated Value) is checked against the same storage budget before DOM creation or refresh; accepted documents therefore do not defer that rejection until rendering. Native form minLength/maxLength constraints retain HTML UTF-16 semantics; they do not redefine the global string contract.
